key_insight: The paper learns to generate realistic polycrystalline microstructures by combining flow matching with graph neural networks over anisotropic power-diagram representations, while enforcing 4-fold rotational symmetry.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, resolution-flexible synthesis of microstructure samples for materials design and analysis, reducing reliance on costly EBSD measurements.
method: Represent each microstructure as an anisotropic power diagram graph.
Train a flow-matching generative model with a $C_4$-equivariant GNN backbone.
Use training-free guidance to steer generation toward target microstructure styles.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful generation of microstructures resembling copper welds, cast metal slabs, 3D-printed stainless steel, and heterogeneous lamella titanium.
watch_item: Quality depends on how well the graph parametrization and symmetry assumptions capture real microstructure variability, so unusual textures may be harder to model faithfully.
paper_title: $C_4$-Equivariant Flow Matching on Anisotropic Power-Diagram Graphs for Microstructure Generation
